title: Benign Traffic (No Attack Detected)
description: This profile represents normal, legitimate network traffic patterns commonly seen in benign flows: standard protocol handshakes, ordinary application request/response cycles, and routine service traffic. It does not itself determine whether any specific flow is an attack or not — it is one of several candidate patterns a flow's SHAP signature may resemble, to be weighed against the other retrieved matches and the flow's own primary evidence (SHAP attribution values, traffic charts) rather than treated as a default or preferred conclusion.

key_features: Feature values within normal operating range for the service/port involved
No sustained burst or flood pattern
Flag combinations consistent with standard protocol handshakes
network_indicators.traffic_pattern: Traffic volume, packet timing, and flag composition fall within the range typically seen for legitimate application traffic on the observed port/protocol.

mitigation.name: No Action Required
mitigation.action: This is expected legitimate traffic. If Layer 1 repeatedly flags this pattern, consider tuning the anomaly threshold or retraining on more representative benign samples.

false_positive_hints: Common causes of Layer 1 false positives that should map here: legitimate but bursty application traffic, misconfigured clients producing atypical (but non-malicious) flag combinations, or benign flows on ports also used by known attack signatures (e.g., SSH management traffic on port 22 resembling brute-force feature patterns).
